notes: Semantic column recognition catalogue (Phase 5.4). DATA: names (EN/FR) a column may carry, value profiles a field accepts (best first), structural families (regex), concept-map relation it belongs to.

Seeded from core/src/mapping.ts SOURCE_FIELDS (union across Shopify/WooCommerce/Wix/BigCommerce/BigBuy) + FR/EN aliases. Paths are the legacy canon keys used by the current parsers; the generic parser (5.5) maps them onto @eloshon/catalog paths.
Adding a field or an alias here never changes the default output — semantic recognition is opt-in (mapping.recognize = "semantic").

Phase 6.3: `derivations` = canonical fields filled from OTHER canonical fields when the source left them empty (applied by the generic parser and by the engine finishing step; provenance method structural + the rule transform). Identifier fields (identifiers.*) and the translations family are recognised as columns; `barcode` keeps the platform column names (Variant Barcode, UPC/EAN, GTIN…) so exact platform rules still win.

fields.notes: Columns suffixed by a locale (name_en, Title (fr), description_nl-BE) are ONE structural family: the default locale stays in the flat fields, the others land in translations[locale].

6.5: a Shopify export column `<label> (product.metafields.<ns>.<key>)` is the metafields family whatever its label; the namespace decides ownership (recognition.v1.json#metafieldOwnership). A metafield holds any value type: no value profile contradicts the carry.
The technical id the SOURCE gave the product (a scraped site, a post id). Kept for traceability; never the target id.
The address of the product page the data was read from. No store imports it as such: kept with the product (sourceExtension) and listed, never written as a handle.

Technical sheet / features. By default APPENDED to the description as a titled section (every platform carries it, nothing is cut into attributes); the user can re-point it to a custom field or attributes.
In stock / out of stock as the source states it (schema.org InStock…), distinct from a quantity. Carried as a custom field.
The teaser beside the price (WooCommerce "Short description"); bodyHtml stays the long text.
A percent (21), not the amount of tax and not a tax class name.
Price per unit of measure (what a shelf label shows), not the selling price; the unit comes from the column name.

derivations.notes: P3 (6.1 A5): when the source splits its identifiers and has no single barcode, barcode = the first available in this order. Never overwrites a native barcode.
7.4: the flat legacy `number` = the immutable source number (a REFERENCE for the target, never its sequence).
7.2: the legacy flat e-mail = the order customer reference e-mail.
7.2: typed status feeds the legacy string.
7.2: provider REFERENCE of the first payment.
7.2: customer phone falls back to the default address phone.
